title: Landform sequence diagram sheet
subject: Geography
source: Written for geography/y7 lesson 17 (Landform sequence diagram sheet (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 17: River landforms and the Thames Estuary. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Meanders
points: Fast water on the outside: erosion
Slow water on the inside: deposition

model.title: How does an ox-bow lake form?

parts.text: Erosion on outer bends narrows the neck
In a flood the river cuts through the neck
Deposition seals the ends of the old bend

panels.title: The Thames Estuary
points: Wide mouth to the North Sea

keywords.def: where a river drops over a step of hard rock
a lake left when a meander is cut off
flat land beside a river that floods
the wide mouth of a river where fresh water meets the sea

questions.q: Explain why the inside of a meander has a slip-off slope. (2 marks)
questions.a: Water is slower on the inside (1), so the river deposits sediment there (1)

questions.q: Core: Draw a four-stage sequence diagram of either a waterfall or an ox-bow lake with explanations.
questions.a: Four correct stages with processes named

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box, describe the Thames Estuary and why it matters.
questions.a: Wide mouth, mudflats, salt marsh, birds, shipping, ports

questions.q: Stretch: Why does a waterfall move upstream over time?
questions.a: Undercutting causes collapse, so the step retreats

questions.q: On a meander, erosion is greatest on the:
questions.a: B) Outside bend. Water flows fastest on the outside bend, so erosion is greatest there.

questions.q: An ox-bow lake forms from a:
Big question: why do rivers wiggle?
questions.a: Faster water erodes outer bends while slower water deposits on inner bends, so bends grow
